prompt: Close-up of a German home-style pork tenderloin goulash, served beside a golden fried grated-potato cake on a plain white deep plate. A creamy, softly light-beige, medium-thick cream sauce loosely coats bite-size cubes of lean pork tenderloin, 1–2 cm, with an even golden-brown fried crust and clearly pale tender meat inside, not dark beef goulash. On top sit soft translucent golden onion dice, smooth tan-brown mushroom halves with darker gills, crisp wavy mahogany-brown bacon shards and bright yellow-olive-green glistening gherkin batons. Next to it one round crisp golden-brown fried grated-potato cake, about 10 cm, with loose lacy shredded-potato strands and darker browned crispy edges. Slight steam, natural fatty sheen, clean plate rim, narrowly blurred table strip, warm soft natural side light, 85 mm lens, f/5.6, true-to-life colours, professional magazine food photo.

visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: Boiled the day before, peeled, coarsely grated and pan-fried in clarified butter into round rösti cakes, about 10–12 cm across and roughly 1,5 cm thick per person; golden brown with darker crisp lacy edges and clearly visible loose shredded-potato strands; rough handmade texture, not a uniform smooth hash brown.

Cut into bite-size cubes of 1–2 cm and seared about 5 minutes in bacon fat; lean, uniformly tender pale meat with an even golden-brown fried crust, clearly light grey and juicy, never dark fibrous beef goulash; roughly 20–25 cubes per portion, mostly coated in sauce.
Diced and sautéed in the pan fat until soft and translucent; small pale golden-glassy pieces with rounded edges, no bite left.
Pan-fried until very crisp, then broken into rough thumbnail-size pieces; crinkled and wavy, medium to dark mahogany brown with slightly darker reddish streaks along the rind edge.
Halved or quartered brown button mushrooms, sautéed soft; smooth tan to medium brown caps, slightly darker gill edges where cut, glossy surface from the pan fat.
Cut into batons 4–5 cm long and about 0,5 cm thick; bright yellow-olive green with smooth glistening skin and translucent flesh, unmistakably pickled gherkins, not fresh cucumber.

visible_ingredients.name_de: Sauce aus Weißwein, Bratensauce und Sauerrahm
visible_ingredients.real_life_appearance: White wine and brown gravy base simmered down, then sour cream stirred in: a creamy, softly light-beige, medium-thick cream sauce with a gentle sheen that loosely coats meat, mushrooms and gherkin batons without burying them.
